rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed Oct 28 hold ~93%, Dec hike >80%; BoC Oct 28 hike ~75–80% (TD, Rabobank: hold); RBNZ Oct 28 hike ~87%; ECB Oct 29 hold ~95%; BoJ Oct 30 hold ~98%; RBA Nov 3 ~50%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~94%; US 2Y ~4.70%
rows.read: Five central banks decide this week, and most still lean toward raising rates because energy keeps inflation high. Canada and New Zealand are expected to hike; the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of Japan are expected to hold, with the Fed and the Bank of Japan seen hiking in December. Investors favoured the dollar on Monday, betting the Fed keeps that December hike in view.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Germany Ifo Oct 90.2 (90.0 fc); UK CBI retail Oct −10 (−47 fc); Chicago Fed activity Sep +0.07 (−0.10 fc); Dallas Fed mfg Oct 13.4 (~7 fc), new orders 9.3 from 30.7
rows.read: Monday's surveys were better than feared. German firms are more hopeful, UK retailers saw sales fall far less than expected, and Texas factories reported more activity, though their new orders slowed sharply. None of it moved currencies much before a week full of central-bank decisions.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Brent $115.81 (−0.8%); Dallas Fed prices paid 55.3 (from 52.2); Japan core CPI Sep 2.1%; UK CPI Sep 3.5%; Australia Q3 CPI Tue 7:30 PM CT
rows.read: Energy is still the main reason inflation runs above target in most big economies, and oil barely fell on Monday. Texas factories also said the prices they pay kept rising. Australia's inflation figures on Tuesday evening, CT, are the week's first big test.

rows.title: Risk
rows.figure: US stocks recover last week's losses (Oct 26); USD/JPY 157.50 (+0.4%); USD/CHF 0.8275 (+0.3%); gold ~$4,033
rows.read: Markets were calm: US stocks won back last week's losses and regional envoys met Iran's leaders to head off new fighting. That cut demand for safe havens, so the yen and the franc weakened. Fresh attacks or failed talks would quickly reverse that.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent $115.81 settle (−0.8%); WTI $101.76 (−1.5%); Houthi claim on Saudi East-West pipeline unconfirmed
rows.read: Oil eased only slightly as the talks in Tehran ended without a deal, so most of the war premium is still in the price. That keeps pressure on energy importers like Japan and the euro area and still supports Canada. The yen felt it most on Monday.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD (sharply added) and EUR (added), for GBP (real money strongly against), for AUD (real money strongly against), leaning against JPY (flipped), strongly for gold (trimmed)
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and the kiwi, even though both central banks are expected to hike this week, so those bets are exposed if the hikes come with signals of more. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Moody's held France at Aa3, negative outlook (Oct 23); French revenue-section first reading postponed; UK Budget Wed Oct 28 ~7:30 AM CT
rows.read: Pressure on France eased after Moody's held its rating, though the first parliamentary vote on France's budget revenues has been postponed. Britain's first Budget from Chancellor John Healey on Wednesday is the bigger test: heavier borrowing could unsettle UK bonds and the pound.
